newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Canada nab group hoping to sell arms to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Canada nab group hoping to sell arms to Iraq.

text.p: Two Americans and a Canadian were arrested last week for plotting to export U.S. military helicopters equipped for chemical warfare to Iraq, U.S. and Canadian authorities said on Monday.

The Americans, both former U.S. military officers, were duped into acting as brokers in a hoax "deal" set up by U.S. Customs which they believed would result in the sale of 34 OH-58A Bell helicopters valued at $12.5 million to Iraq, officials said.
Robert Fairchild, 52, of Little Rock, Ark., and Donald Proven, 55, of Chicago, were arrested July 18 on charges of conspiracy and violations of the U.S. Arms Export Control Act, officials said.
The two appeared in U.S. District court on Monday and were held on $125,000 bond each.
On July 19, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police arrested Gary Finlay, 47, of Bloomfield, Ontario, Canada, the owner of the helicopters. He faced similar charges under Canadian law.
The deal was set up through an elaborate U.S. Customs "sting" operation. Customs agents learned that the helicopters were available through an informant, a spokesman said.

Investigators said the helicopters were originally sold to the Canadian government and then to a "private entity" in Canada. It remained illegal to export the aircraft out of Canada without U.S. government permission, officials said.

Fairchild, a former Army colonel, and Proven, a former Marine, dealt with U.S. undercover agents and were led to believe the helicopters were being bought for shipment to Iraq, U.S. Customs agent Keith Prager said.
"It is unfortunate that sometimes greed overtakes whatever patriotism someone might have had," Prager said.

The two devised a scheme to supply false documents to the U.S. State Department, indicating the helicopters were destined for an aviation company in the Philippines, a front established for the illegal sale, he said.
The helicopters could have been equipped to fire rockets in addition to chemical weapons, officials said.
